title: JSON schema conditional rules do not enforce required fields when defaulted grounding modes are omitted
reasoning: The exported JSON schema advertises default manual grounding, but the conditional rules only apply when find_coordinates_by or drag_to_find_coordinates_by is explicitly present. JSON Schema validators generally do not materialize defaults before evaluating if/then rules, so a payload can omit find_coordinates_by and x/y, or omit drag_to_find_coordinates_by and drag_to_x/drag_to_y for a drag action, while still passing the published schema. The Pydantic runtime defaults those modes to manual and then rejects the same payload. That creates a contract mismatch between model-facing tool schemas and backend runtime validation, causing avoidable tool-call failures for payloads that conform to the published schema.
recommendation: Make the JSON schema rules match runtime defaults. For source grounding, require x/y whenever find_coordinates_by is absent or manual. For drag destination grounding, require drag_to_x/drag_to_y when action is drag and drag_to_find_coordinates_by is absent or manual. Alternatively, make the mode fields required in the JSON schema instead of relying on defaults.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for these schema builders or for parity between generated JSON schema validation and Pydantic validation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a schema-parity test that validates example payloads against the generated JSON schema and the corresponding Pydantic models, including omitted find_coordinates_by and omitted drag_to_find_coordinates_by on drag actions. Assert both layers reject missing manual coordinates consistently.
minimumFixScope: Update the JSON schema conditional rules in backend/src/tools/computer/grounding_contract.py and add focused parity coverage for MouseControlArgs and any tool schema that consumes these helper rules.
